priceSnapshot.note: The overnight did the opposite of what the endday expected, and the distinction between the two moves is the whole story. The endday closed at 64,912.3 calling for a test of the 64,750 long-liquidation shelf. That test never came. The low since that snapshot is 64,826.2, which left 76.2 points of air above the shelf and 176.2 above the 64,650 reduce line, and from there price has climbed six straight hours to 65,265.1 - up 352.8 points, +0.54%, on the endday reference. The 01:00Z hourly bar ran to 65,388.0, matching the 07 August range high to the tick, and failed. But the 06:00Z bar then closed at 65,297.3, which is the highest settled HOURLY CLOSE of the week and sits 2.7 points beneath the add trigger the midday session set eighteen hours ago. Twice now the range top has rejected a wick; this is the first time price has come back and built a close underneath it instead of collapsing away from it.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $64,650 - held UNCHANGED for a TWELFTH consecutive session, and the clearance has widened again rather than narrowed. Spot 65,265.1 leaves 615.1 points, 0.94%, which is 0.45 of a daily ATR against the 0.19 the endday reported. The endday was right to describe the line as no longer remote and wrong about which way price would travel to reach it; the honest reading is that the line was never tested. What stands between price and the trigger has rebuilt from three levels to seven: the 15m EMA200 at 65,015.48, the 1H EMA50 at 65,005.91, the sodUtc0 open at 64,899.2, the 4H EMA20 at 64,857.31, the 1H EMA100 at 64,826.56 which is now within a point of the overnight low at 64,826.2, the $814,828 long-liquidation shelf at 64,800, and the daily EMA50 at 64,683.13. The line stays where it is for the same structural reason it has stayed for eleven prior sessions - a settled hourly close beneath 64,650 loses the daily EMA50 - and there is no case for moving it up while the range top remains unbroken.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $65,300, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. Held UNCHANGED for a THIRD session because the condition is doing exactly the work it was written to do, and tonight it separated the two halves for the first time. The PRICE half has not fired: the 06:00Z bar closed at 65,297.3, 2.7 points short, and no settled hourly close this week has cleared the level. The OPEN-INTEREST half is now SATISFIED and was not at the failed breakout - OI has RISEN 0.50% from $2,056,643,157 to $2,067,023,377 across the six-hour advance, where it FELL 1.66% across the 22:00Z breakout that the endday correctly refused to buy. That is the difference between a squeeze completing and a market being accumulated, and for the first time in this range the second reading is the live one. This is the fourth consecutive test of the open-interest rule and the fourth time it has scored, so it is retained verbatim.

decisionBox.changed: Position flips from REDUCE back to ADD and the tilt from bearish to bullish, reversing the endday one session after it was set. The endday's reasoning was sound on the evidence in front of it and its four flip signals have all since reversed, which is the honest way to describe what happened rather than calling it a bad read. Open interest was FALLING 1.66% then and is RISING 0.50% now. The 1H MACD histogram was -13.60 and is +3.77. 1H RSI was 40.42 and is 60.55. Funding was 0.00912% per 8h and has HALVED to 0.00732%, so the long crowding that worried the endday has bled off rather than built. Only one signal did not reverse: the long/short account ratio is 1.24 against 1.22, its highest of the week, and that is the single reason this is an ADD with a partial tranche rather than a full deployment. Price is above every 15m, 1H and 4H moving average and above the daily EMA20 and EMA50, but it is also 123 points beneath a range top that has now rejected wicks twice in eight hours. The reduce line and add trigger are both untouched for a twelfth and third session respectively.

liquidityMagnet.note: The pull has flipped back from down to UP, and it flipped because the participation test that failed eight hours ago now passes. Composition: the three bands above spot at 65,300, 65,350 and 65,450 hold $1,490,518 that is 99.99% SHORT-side, all of it consumed on the two failed pushes - spent fuel, which argues the ceiling is real. But the bands immediately below spot at 65,250, 65,200 and 65,150 hold $803,605 that is 97% short as well, and those were created in the last six hours as price climbed THROUGH them. Short liquidations above and below means the market is walking up over a floor of covering, not being distributed into. Participation: open interest ROSE 0.50% from $2,056,643,157 to $2,067,023,377 across the advance, the exact inverse of the 1.66% contraction the endday measured across the breakout. Contracts are being opened into this move. Funding: HALVED from 0.00912% to 0.00732% per 8h - longs still pay shorts, but half as urgently, so the advance is not being financed by leverage. One measure dissents: the long/short account ratio is 1.24, the week's high, up from 1.22. The crowd is longer than it was and that is a real vulnerability. Three of four measures point up and the honest nearest genuine magnet is 65,300, but 64,800 - $814,828 and 92.6% long - is where a failure would be aimed and it is the largest live shelf either side of the market.

calibration.rollingRecord: 62 rows on file before this one. The 09 Aug endday called range with a bearish tilt at 27/43/30 from 64,912.3, flipped position from ADD to REDUCE, held the reduce at 64,650 for an eleventh session and held the add trigger at 65,300 for a second. It scores as a clean directional miss with sound process. The DIRECTION was wrong: price is 65,265.1, up 352.8 points or +0.54% on the endday reference, and the trim it executed sold spot into what turned out to be the low of the overnight. Its central prediction - that 64,750 would be tested before 65,000 was reclaimed - failed on both counts. 65,000 was reclaimed at 04:00Z and 64,750 was never approached; the lowest trade since the snapshot is 64,826.2, leaving 76.2 points of clearance. actingHelped is FALSE. The LEVELS were right for a twelfth and third time and that is not consolation, it is the part of the process that keeps working: 64,650 was never within 176 points, and the 65,300 add trigger did not fire on a 06:00Z close of 65,297.3 that missed by 2.7 points - a close that would have bought 35 points under the trigger had the trigger been naked. What the endday could not know is that its own four flip signals would all reverse inside six hours. Open interest went from -1.66% to +0.50%, the 1H histogram from -13.60 to +3.77, RSI from 40.42 to 60.55 and funding halved. The lesson is not that the endday read the tape badly - it read it correctly - but that a single failed breakout on contracting open interest is evidence about that breakout, not about the six hours after it. The endday seat still carries the desk's best attributed record at +36.01 across fourteen decisions.
calibration.note: One backfill is applied and no other row is touched. The 09 Aug ENDDAY row's price_next_report is set to 65,265.1 and its add_fired is resolved to FALSE - the 65,300 trigger required a settled 1H close and the closest any settled hourly close came was 65,297.3 at 06:00Z, 2.7 points short, so it correctly did not fire for a second consecutive session. Its reduce_fired stands at FALSE and its acting_helped is set to FALSE. The open question the endday handed forward was whether a crowded long book above a growing long-liquidation shelf would flush overnight. It did not, and the reason is visible in the one measure the endday could not see yet: open interest expanded into the recovery instead of contracting into it. The rule the desk carries forward is unchanged and has now scored four times - a level break is only worth acting on when open interest expands into it - but tonight it cuts the other way for the first time, because the condition is now SATISFIED and the price half is 2.7 points away. The morning session inherits a trigger that is closer to firing than it has ever been and an account ratio at its weekly high underneath it.
